scope: Bounded removal of regenerable Python bytecode inside existing platform release virtual environments; source, packages, release directories and rollback paths retained.
checks: Fixed platform release root; only regular nonsymlink *.pyc directly in __pycache__ under each .venv are candidates.
Canonical importlib.util.source_from_cache maps standard and optimized cache names to the actual corresponding source; invalid or sourceless bytecode is skipped.
Release/venv/manifest symlinks are excluded at scan; candidate/source links and inner symlink ancestors are excluded. Candidate resolved path must remain inside its virtual environment.
Before unlink, target device/inode/size/mtime, source existence/hash, inner ancestors and path containment are checked again. Changed candidates are skipped; changed manifests abort.
Manifest must not declare virtual-environment bytecode; corresponding source hashes and manifest bytes are verified unchanged after each release.
No source, package metadata, native module, database, credential, application setting, report, release directory or active tool cache is a deletion target.
Existing active relevant services must still be active after cleanup. Measured filesystem free-space delta is reported separately from unlinked allocation totals.
Final source parses successfully; no full regression suite is needed for removal of regenerable cache files.
resolved_comments: Replaced manual filename split with canonical source_from_cache.
Added source/hash/path/manifest revalidation immediately before unlink.
limitations: Approval assumes the existing release directories and source packages remain immutable during this maintenance; concurrent deployments moving/replacing release directory trees are outside this scope.
Service-state comparison establishes active units, not browser/UI or acoustic acceptance.
No remote execution or cleanup performed by reviewer; post-cleanup evidence remains to be collected by the executor.
